text:
Jordan: quick heads-up 1 1 proposal: tighten postmortem follow-ups. idea dump below, want feedback before I put in the runbook.
Tess: curious. short bullets pls. :memo:
Jordan: ok TL;DR: 1) require assignment of a follow-up owner within 2h of incident close 2) action assignment SLA buckets (P0=7d, P1=30d, P2=90d) 3) add a 48h "stabilizer" role to own triage for first 48h post-close 4) weekly recurrence heatmap + owner review.
Leah: +1 to stabilizer role. experienced too many incidents closed with nobody babysitting reappearing alerts.
Devon: can we make the follow-up-owner different from the person who files the postmortem? avoids bias and spreads ownership.
Jordan: yes that's the plan. follow-up-owner should be from the service team but not the reporter when possible.
Tess: what does stabilizer do exactly?
Jordan: short list: monitor for re-fires, confirm action items are assigned, triage false positives, update incident doc with new findings. basically a 48h babysitter.
Leah: communications cadence suggestion: while incident active -> updates every 20m (1 line). after close & during stabilizer window -> summary at 6h and 24h, then daily until stabilizer ends.
Devon: also add a required single-line "closure rationale" on close (what changed to mark recovered). helps later triage.
oncall-bot: auto-template available: /incident handoff will output a structured snippet.
Jordan: propose an "IC shadow" for each 4hr rotation during active windows. shadow watches for context loss and takes over documentation handoff. means shorter IC shifts are safer.
Tess: sounds good. we should make handoffs a single-post in channel rather than multi-message so it's easy to copy into docs.
Jordan: mock handoff template (keep very small):
```
Handoff: [1 line summary]
State: [mitigating/recovered/degraded]
Top actions: 1)desc (owner, ETA) 2)desc (owner, ETA)
Open alarms: [brief list]
Closure rationale (if closing): [1 line]
Follow-up owner: [name]
Stabilizer end: [time UTC]
Links: [inc doc, dashboards]
```
Leah: nice. make 'Follow-up owner' mandatory before close button enabled in our tooling.
Devon: for tracking I want a tiny "postmortem backlog" table exposed as CSV with columns: id, incident_ts, brief, owner, severity, due, status, recurrence_count. weekly export to owners.
Tess: recurrence detection: algorithm idea: group by error strings + top-3 affected endpoints + deploy tag. produce a weekly "recurrence digest" with number of similar incidents and sample timestamps. repo owners should get a digest.
Jordan: governance: add a 2-week remediation review meeting for all P0/P1 remediations to confirm progress and de-risk. 
Leah: add a "closure sanity check" where a second engineer must ack the closure rationale for high-sev incidents. prevents rush closings.
Devon: operationally, we can enforce assignment SLA with oncall-bot: if no follow-up owner in 2h -> DM incident manager and post in channel. if no owner in 24h escalate to team lead.
oncall-bot: If follow-up owner not assigned after 2h, will DM @incident-manager. If not assigned after 24h, will @channel escalate.
Tess: what about action item aging? weekly reminders to owners with overdue actions and a rolling 30d public list for exec visibility.
Jordan: yes add public rolling list for >30d actions (only summary lines, not sensitive data). helps pressure but keeps details internal.
Leah: timeline templates: attach 3 templates in runbook: short incident (resolved <4h), medium (4h-48h), major (>48h). each template has required fields and different cadence rules.
Devon: assignables for next steps:
- Jordan: write runbook PR with templates + closure flow change (due 4d)
- Tess: build recurrence digest spec (due 6d)
- Leah: add stabilizer duties and ownership ladder to oncall playbook (due 3d)
- Devon: wire basic CSV export and bot escalation (due 1w)
Tess: assigning owners now in the thread. I'll start the digest proto and ping infra for logs correlation.
Leah: I'll draft the closure sanity check UI copy for the incident tool.
Jordan: one minor ask 1 when we close incidents, please add a single tag with root-cause category (service/downstream/deploy/config/infra/perf). this will help the weekly heatmap.
Devon: noted. I'll add the tag field to the CSV export.
Tess: ok let's run this as a 4-week pilot starting next Monday. measure: percent of incidents with follow-up-owner set within 2h, recurrence count change, and overdue actions.
Jordan: agreed. I'll open the pilot signup and move runbook PR to draft. thanks all. :raised_hands:
